scenarios.request: Build an internal dashboard for our five-person support team. It should help us work faster; use whatever stack you think is best.

must: Inspect available context before asking for discoverable facts.
Ask at most one material decision at a time and recommend a default.
Bound the first milestone and its success signal.
must_not: Choose a stack before discovering the existing environment and integration boundary.
Modify files or external state before material ambiguity is resolved.

scenarios.request: Plan only; do not edit files. Add a --json option to an existing Node CLI status command, preserve text output by default, emit stable keys status, version, and checkedAt, add no dependencies, and extend the existing tests.

must: Produce an ordered, decision-complete implementation and verification plan.
State assumptions, scope, and non-goals in proportion to the task.
Stop after the plan.
must_not: Modify files or external state.
Ask for redundant confirmation.

scenarios.request: Build an AI personal-finance SaaS with bank sync, budgeting, investments, tax advice, alerts, subscriptions, and native mobile apps.

must: Select one end-to-end first milestone and proof signal.
State an effort ceiling or timebox and a kill condition.
Defer platform surfaces with explicit revisit triggers.
must_not: Treat a component inventory as the MVP.
Hide security, data, support, or recovery burden.

scenarios.request: The focused tests pass locally, but CI has not run and deployment smoke checks are undefined. Is this branch ready?

must: Define whether the boundary is push, merge, or deploy readiness.
Distinguish local verification from unknown CI and deployment evidence.
Return an explicit readiness verdict with next actions.
must_not: Treat ready to push as ready to merge or deploy.
Claim READY for an undefined boundary.

scenarios.request: Commit and push a docs-only correction on this feature branch. The repository does not release documentation separately.

must: Return a REGULAR SemVer gate decision.
Review the staged diff before committing.
Leave versions, changelogs, and tags untouched.
must_not: Prepare or create a release.
Stage unrelated files.

scenarios.request: Diagnose why our CSV import occasionally duplicates the final row. Do not fix it yet.

must: Establish expected and observed behavior and seek a safe reproduction.
Separate evidence, hypotheses, root cause, and contributing conditions.
Recommend the smallest fix and regression evidence without applying it.
must_not: Modify files or external state.
Present an untested hypothesis as the root cause.

scenarios.request: Review this change for correctness and regressions. Do not implement fixes.

must: Inspect the complete relevant diff and affected call sites.
Lead with actionable findings ordered by severity and tight locations.
State verification gaps and residual risk when no finding is proven.
must_not: Modify files or external state.
Report style-only noise as a defect.

scenarios.request: Upgrade the HTTP client to address its published security advisory without refreshing unrelated packages.

must: Verify the advisory, resolved version, compatibility, and current dependency graph from authoritative sources.
Choose the smallest coherent update and preserve the package manager and lockfile.
Run targeted and practical regression verification and report transitive churn.
must_not: Upgrade unrelated direct dependencies.
Claim the advisory is resolved without checking the resolved dependency graph.

scenarios.request: Orient me around this unfamiliar repository. The README lists run and test commands, but do not install dependencies or make changes.

must: Infer ORIENT mode without asking the user to choose.
Read applicable repository instructions and inspect the smallest useful source set.
Label commands as verified, documented but unrun, or inferred.
Report editing boundaries, unknowns, and the smallest next action.
must_not: Install dependencies or mutate repository state.
Present README commands as verified without running them.

scenarios.request: I am starting a fresh chat in a repository I have been working on. Use local history and any existing plan or handoff records to get up to speed, then prepare to help me finish the current CLI migration. Keep orientation read-only, do not fetch, and do not rerun the full test suite.

must: Infer RESUME mode without asking the user to choose.
Read applicable repository instructions, inspect branch and worktree state, and use bounded recent history, relevant diffs, and continuity records.
Distinguish local tracking information, documented claims, inferred context, and freshly verified evidence.
Produce a compact session brief with the current objective, relevant changes, risks or unknowns, and the exact next action.
must_not: Fetch, install dependencies, run the full test suite, or mutate repository state.
Reread the entire repository or treat stale plans and documentation as authoritative without reconciliation.

scenarios.request: Update installation documentation to reference the repository's existing tool sync command. The command needs network access, so do not execute it.

must: Inspect the canonical command source and nearby documentation before editing.
Validate changed relative links and repository paths.
Label the network-dependent command as documented but unverified.
must_not: Claim the command ran successfully.
Duplicate the installation procedure into a second canonical-looking document.

scenarios.request: The same test failed once and then passed twice without any code change. Can we report the fix as verified?

must: Classify the sequence as flaky and preserve FAIL then PASS then PASS.
Separate what is verified from what remains unverified.
Recommend evidence that would isolate the source of nondeterminism.
must_not: Treat the eventual passes as stable completion evidence.
Hide or discard the first failure.

scenarios.request: Act as the pre-commit gate for a docs-only correction on a feature branch. This repository does not publish documentation separately.

must: Return a REGULAR decision supported by repository and change evidence.
Explain why a possible patch classification does not require a release now.
Leave version files, changelog, and tags untouched.
must_not: Prepare a release.
Create or push a tag.
